headline: Actor Riaz denied bail in two cases by High Court
summary: The court returned the actor's anticipatory bail applications, removing them from the cause list.
details: The High Court has returned the anticipatory bail applications of actor Riaz in connection with two separate cases.
A bench comprising Justice K M Zahid Sarwar and Justice Sheikh Abu Taher gave the order on Thursday.
Riaz had applied for anticipatory bail in two cases filed at Jatrabari and Shahbagh police stations in Dhaka.
The court did not grant bail and instead returned the applications, deleting them from the the cause list.
Deputy Attorney General Monjurul Alam Sujon confirmed that the actor was present in court during the proceedings.
caption:
Actor Riaz's bid for anticipatory bail in two separate cases has been rejected by the High Court.

The High Court has returned the anticipatory bail applications of actor Riaz in connection with two separate cases.

A bench comprising Justice K M Zahid Sarwar and Justice Sheikh Abu Taher gave the order on Thursday.

Riaz had applied for anticipatory bail in two cases filed at Jatrabari and Shahbagh police stations in Dhaka.

The court did not grant bail and instead returned the applications, deleting them from the the cause list.

Deputy Attorney General Monjurul Alam Sujon confirmed that the actor was present in court during the proceedings.

headline: 32.78% of bank loans: Bangladesh now world's highest in default loans
summary: Out of every 100 Taka distributed as loans, nearly 33 Taka are now defaulted, pushing the country to the top of the global list.
details: Bangladesh has become the world's leading country in terms of default loan rates. According to Bangladesh Bank, by the end of June 2026, default loans in the banking sector reached 6.06 trillion Taka, accounting for 32.78% of total distributed loans.

The surge is attributed to the revelation of irregular, anonymous, and fraudulent loans that were previously hidden through rescheduling and special waivers during the previous Awami League government's tenure.

Following political changes, audits by domestic and foreign agencies have exposed the true extent of the crisis. Five merged banks are in the worst condition, with over 80% of their loans being defaulted.
Other contributing factors include political influence in loan distribution, weak supervision, economic downturns, and energy crises.
Bangladesh now leads a list that includes Chad (31.51%), Equatorial Guinea (30%), Algeria (20.05%), and Ghana (18.11%), based on the latest available IMF and other financial data.

Ukraine, which previously held the top spot with rates as high as 39%, has significantly reduced its default rate to 12.5% by July 2026 through loan recovery, restructuring, and the write-off of old defaulted loans.
While Ukraine improved its situation, Bangladesh's official default loans grew from 2.11 trillion Taka in June 2024 to over 6 trillion Taka within two years.
caption:
Nearly 33% of all bank loans in Bangladesh are now defaulted, making the country the world leader in loan defaults.

Bangladesh has become the world's leading country in terms of default loan rates. According to Bangladesh Bank, by the end of June 2026, default loans in the banking sector reached 6.06 trillion Taka, accounting for 32.78% of total distributed loans.

The surge is attributed to the revelation of irregular, anonymous, and fraudulent loans that were previously hidden through rescheduling and special waivers during the previous Awami League government's tenure.

Following political changes, audits by domestic and foreign agencies have exposed the true extent of the crisis. Five merged banks are in the worst condition, with over 80% of their loans being defaulted.

Other contributing factors include political influence in loan distribution, weak supervision, economic downturns, and energy crises.

Bangladesh now leads a list that includes Chad (31.51%), Equatorial Guinea (30%), Algeria (20.05%), and Ghana (18.11%), based on the latest available IMF and other financial data.

Ukraine, which previously held the top spot with rates as high as 39%, has significantly reduced its default rate to 12.5% by July 2026 through loan recovery, restructuring, and the write-off of old defaulted loans.

While Ukraine improved its situation, Bangladesh's official default loans grew from 2.11 trillion Taka in June 2024 to over 6 trillion Taka within two years.
